survivors.claim: Commit eee36a4 (in range, HEAD) drops per-layer agentMap routing from the WAVE step: `const agent = layerAgent` where `layerAgent = agentMap.default || 'general-purpose'` replaces `agentMap[layer] || agentMap.default || 'general-purpose'`, so every layer now prints the default agent regardless of the host's agentMap. No Decision in specs/20260910/08 sanctions this hunk (D1–D12 touch runGate/staging, the integration sentence, the header, ADR/doc prose, bump, ratchet, .DS_Store), the commit subject ('route each wave layer through the host agent map') describes the opposite of what the diff does, and it contradicts specs/20260901/01-build-driver.md line 146: 'The WAVE step prints, per layer in the wave: the `agentMap` subagent type'. The size-baseline.json growth in the same commit (+13 bytes on the driver) was reconciled citing this spec for an unrelated regression.
survivors.impact: On any host whose config maps a layer to a dedicated worker kind, the build driver now tells the session to dispatch the default agent for that layer instead, silently mis-routing every wave worker; the change rides in under this spec's name with nothing in the spec asking for it.
survivors.evidence: Executed: fixture host with agentMap {scripts:'gate-scripts', default:'general-purpose'}, one File Plan row `src/created.js | CREATE | scripts`, bare driver invocation at WAVE:doctrine+scripts. Base driver (git show a9134b8:spec/scripts/spec-build-driver.js, lib requires pointed at the untouched lib dir): `BASE:   layer: scripts  agent: gate-scripts`. HEAD driver: `HEAD:   layer: scripts  agent: general-purpose`. Hunk (git show eee36a4): `-    const agent = agentMap[layer] || agentMap.default || 'general-purpose'` / `+    const agent = layerAgent` with `+  const layerAgent = agentMap.default || 'general-purpose'`. Spec side: specs/20260901/01-build-driver.md:146 'The WAVE step prints, per layer in the wave: the `agentMap` subagent type'. No test in tests/ asserts the printed per-layer agent (grep for `agent: ` across tests/build returned nothing), which is why the suite leg (1625 pass) did not catch it.

survivors.claim: Commit 71b0d23 'build: follow-up' is in the range and only bumps `reviewed:` dates (2026-09-06 → 2026-09-10) in three .claude/agent-memory/**/*.md files; it is not in the File Plan, carries no spec citation, and its subject does not say what it does.
survivors.impact: Harmless metadata churn, but an unlabelled commit inside a spec branch makes the range harder to audit and is the same commit style that let the routing regression above ride in unnoticed.
survivors.evidence: git show 71b0d23: three files, each `-  reviewed: 2026-09-06` / `+  reviewed: 2026-09-10`; reconcile leg reports outOfPlan 0 because agent-memory is outside its walk.
